confirm.ap_restart: The access point restarts with the new name or password: connected devices are cut off and must join it again.

confirm.to_ap: Switch to the standalone access point? The player leaves the venue Wi-Fi: then join the network "{ssid}" and open http://10.42.0.1:8080.
confirm.to_client: Switch to the venue Wi-Fi? The player stops its access point and joins a saved network: you will be disconnected. If none can be reached, the access point comes back within 2 minutes.

Address of the player on this network: http://10.42.0.1:8080. The name and password are also shown on the setup screen.

playlist.hint_many: The media play in order, then the playlist starts over: each video is repeated the number of times shown (seamlessly between repeats), each image stays on screen for the duration shown in seconds.
playlist.hint_single: A single media: it loops forever, seamlessly. Add more media to build a playlist.
playlist.repeat_title: Number of plays in a row
prep.ffmpeg: With ffmpeg, on the command line
prep.ffmpeg_intro: Install ffmpeg, then, in a terminal, replace input.mov with your file:
prep.ffmpeg_result: Result: MP4, H.264, 1080p at most, stereo AAC sound, original resolution and frame rate kept. Above 30 frames/s in 1080p, add -r 30 before output.mp4: the Pi 3 decodes no faster.
prep.handbrake_1: Install HandBrake (Windows, macOS, Linux) and open your video.
prep.handbrake_2: Preset: General › Fast 1080p30. It produces H.264 in MP4 with AAC sound, 1080p and 30 frames/s at most: the player format.
prep.handbrake_4: Start Encode, then upload the .mp4 file you get.
prep.intro: Raspberry Pi 3: convert your videos on your computer before uploading them. The player can do it, but on this model the conversion is slow and saturates the Pi, to the point of disturbing playback. A video already in the right format is stored as is, instantly.
sound.title: Sound
